findings.claim: Net operating cash flow (M9) and debt service cover (M10) count every non-financing credit, including the non-trading inflows the categoriser deliberately sends to OTHER (capital injection, owner/director money in, transfer from savings, grants, unexplained credits). D4 kept them out of revenue (M2) but not out of the DSCR numerator, which is the outcome categorise.py:14 says it was meant to prevent. A one-off capital injection turns an R2 'fail' (on_fail: fail) into a 'pass' while staying under R9's 20% unexplained-inflow limit, so nothing refers it. R8 (M9 > 0, fail) is equally liftable.

findings.claim: The date exemption blanks any month name followed by any 1-2 digit number (days 32-99 included) before numbers are read, and the unit after it is left unread. An invented percentage or count written after a month name passes the guard as grounded, which breaks outcome (a), 'no figure that is not in the metrics table'.
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £120,000 [M2]. In March 62% of transfer revenue came from one payer.', ms).grounded == True; same for 'By September 85 days had closed overdrawn.' (ms = [Metric M2 120000 GBP]).

findings.claim: The Monzo importer calls describe() without the payment reference (Monzo's Description / Notes column), although describe() takes an `extra` argument for it. Every invoice reference is dropped, so no Monzo transfer can ever be REVENUE_TRANSFER: customer payments become OTHER, M2 drops to card settlements only (usually £0 on Monzo), and M15 is always n/a, so R7 passes through when_missing: pass. The memo then quotes a cited, grounded and wrong 'Total revenue'.
findings.repro: Monzo CSV row 'tx_1,01/10/2025,...,Faster payment,Acme Trading Ltd,...,2400.00,...,INV1041 (Notes),...,INV1041 (Description)' converts to 'FPS CREDIT ACME TRADING LTD' and categorises as other; same for a Bacs credit with 'INVOICE 2210'. See /tmp/claude-0/-home-claude/2adee499-4534-5c98-9209-a2ce9b0b4719/scratchpad/panel03/staff/monzo_in.csv.

findings.claim: LIST_MARKER exempts any integer of any length at the start of a line followed by '.' or ')' and whitespace, with no list context. A hard-wrapped memo whose line begins with an invented figure ending a sentence is skipped.
findings.repro: guard.check('Revenue was £120,000 [M2] and the business also owes HMRC\n45000. That is a concern.', ms).grounded == True

findings.claim: The evidence file name does not depend on the decision: a rejected re-run to the same --out writes NAME.rejected.md but overwrites NAME.evidence.json, which then sits beside the earlier approved NAME.md and describes a different draft (memo text, guard result, review).
findings.repro: cma run s.csv --reviewer A --yes --out m.md (writes m.md, m.evidence.json); re-run interactively, reject: m.rejected.md written and m.evidence.json replaced; m.md unchanged.

findings.claim: M3 divides total revenue, including revenue dated in a boundary month that covered_months() dropped, by the number of covered months only, so average monthly revenue is overstated whenever a short first or last month has takings.
findings.repro: Statement from 2025-10-19 to 2026-10-31 with a 20000 card settlement on 2025-10-19 and 10000 a month after: M1 12, M2 140000, M3 11666.67 (the 12 covered months average 10000).

findings.claim: Ground truth covers nine metrics but not M9, M10 or M16, which feed the two 'fail' rules R2 and R8 and the new R9. synth.py never generates a non-trading inflow, so the suite cannot see finding 1. P1's metric list is the requirement most likely to be wrong: it omits the decision-driving ratios.
findings.repro: grep -n 'M9\|M10\|M16' evals/run_evals.py returns nothing; grep -n 'CAPITAL\|SAVINGS\|INJECT' src/cma/synth.py returns nothing.

findings.claim: M4 'Revenue trend' compares the last three covered months with the first three of a roughly 12-month statement, which are opposite seasons. For a seasonal business (the cafe archetype) R6 refers or passes on seasonality, not trend, and the name invites a misreading. Year on year is not computable from 12 months, and that limit is not written down.
findings.repro: Read metrics.py:148-156 and M4's method string; for an Oct-Sep statement first3 is Oct-Dec and last3 is Jul-Sep.

findings.claim: When --opening-balance is supplied, Monzo's own Balance column is never checked (the comparison only runs when source is 'Monzo Balance column'), so a wrong opening balance silently shifts every balance and therefore M5, M6 and R4. _money (line 64) also accepts '1e5' and '1,234', which ingest's strict amounts would refuse.
findings.repro: monzo.convert(monzo_in.csv, out, opening_balance=99999.0) on an export whose Balance column implies an opening balance of 1000 returns balance_source 'opening balance supplied', closing 103699.0, no error.
